questions.question: The Competition (Amendment) Bill, 2022 belongs to ____ Ministry of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Corporate Affairs.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Competition (Amendment) Bill, 2022** aims to amend the **Competition Act, 2002,** which falls under the purview of the **Ministry of Corporate Affairs.**
 
• **The Ministry of Tribal Affairs** primarily deals with matters related to the welfare and development of tribal communities in India.
 
• **The Ministry of Finance** is responsible for the management of public finances, fiscal policy, and economic policy in India.
 
• **The Ministry of Law and Justice** is responsible for the formulation of legal policy and drafting of legislation in India.
 
• **The Competition (Amendment) Bill, 2022** is related to the regulation of competition in the market, which is primarily under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Ministry of Tribal Affairs was created in 1999 to address the unique needs and challenges faced by tribal communities in India.
 
• The Ministry of Finance is one of the most important ministries of the Government of India and is responsible for the management of the country's finances.
 
• The Ministry of Law and Justice is responsible for the administration of justice and the development of legal institutions in India.
 
• The Competition Act, 2002 was enacted to promote competition in the market and to prevent anti-competitive practices.

***Hence, the statement "The Competition (Amendment) Bill, 2022 belongs to the Ministry of Corporate Affairs of India" is correct.***

questions.question: The rules made for the Buddhist “Sangha” were written down in a book called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vinaya Pitaka.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Vinaya Pitaka** is a sacred book of Buddhist scripture that contains the **rules and regulations for the Buddhist monastic community or Sangha.**
 
• It is **one of the three Pitakas **or baskets of scriptures that make up the** Tripitaka**, the canonical texts of Theravada Buddhism.
 
• The Vinaya Pitaka is divided into three sections: **Suttavibhanga, Khandhaka, and Parivara.**
 
• The other options are also significant texts in Buddhist scripture.
 
• **Abhidhammapitaka **is the third basket of the Tripitaka that contains** philosophical and psychological teachings**.
 
• **Sutta Pitaka **is the second basket of the Tripitaka that contains the Buddha's teachings in the form of discourses.
 
• **Milinda Panha** is a Buddhist text that records a dialogue between King Milinda and Buddhist monk Nagasena.

***Hence, the statement "The rules made for the Buddhist 'Sangha' were written down in a book called Vinaya Pitaka" is correct.***

questions.question: Which among the following is NOT a bacterial disease?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rabies.**__

__
 
• Rabies is a** viral disease.** It is caused by the** rabies virus, **which belongs to the family** Rhabdoviridae, genus Lyssavirus. **This virus primarily infects mammals, including humans, and it is typically transmitted through the saliva of infected animals, often through bites or scratches. Once symptoms develop, rabies is almost always fatal if left untreated.
 
• **Cholera** is a bacterial disease caused by the **bacterium Vibrio cholerae** and is transmitted through **contaminated water and food.**
 
• **Typhoid** is also a bacterial disease caused by the bacterium Salmonella typhi and is transmitted through **contaminated water and food.**
 
• **Plague is a bacterial disease** caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis and is transmitted through **fleas that infest rodents.**
 
• ***Therefore, the correct answer is option 3, Rabies, as it is a viral disease and not caused by bacteria.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cholera: **Symptoms include diarrhea, vomiting, and dehydration. It can be prevented through proper sanitation and hygiene practices.
 
• **Typhoid:** Symptoms include high fever, weakness, and stomach pain. It can be prevented through vaccination and proper sanitation and hygiene practices.
 
• **Plague:** Symptoms include fever, chills, and swollen lymph nodes. It can be prevented through rodent control and flea control measures.

questions.question: What is another name for frozen carbon dioxide?

__
 
• **Frozen carbon dioxide** is commonly known as** dry ice.**
 
• It is called dry ice because it is **solid carbon dioxide and does not melt** but **sublimates directly from solid to gas.**
 
• Dry ice is used in various industries for** cooling purposes, such as transporting perishable goods, creating smoke and fog effects** in the entertainment industry, and cleaning surfaces.
 
• It is also used in the medical field for **cryotherapy, **which involves the freezing of tissues to remove abnormal growths.

• **Coal** is a fossil fuel formed from the remains of ancient plants. It is not related to frozen carbon dioxide.
 
• **Coke** is a solid fuel made from coal. It is also not related to frozen carbon dioxide.

***Therefore, the correct answer is option 3, Dry Ice.***

questions.question: Which of the following reforms led to the enactment of the Government of India Act of 1919?

• The Government of India Act of 1919, also known as the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, was a significant constitutional reform in British India.
 
• In 1918, Edwin Montagu, the Secretary of State, and Lord Chelmsford, the Viceroy, produced their scheme of constitutional reforms, known as the Montagu-Chelmsford (or Mont-Ford) Reforms, which led to the enactment of the Government of India Act of 1919.
 
• Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms came into force in 1921.
 
• The sole purpose of this Act was to ensure Indians of their representation in the Government.
 
• The Act introduced reforms at the Central and Provincial levels of Government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** The antislavery reforms refer to the movement to abolish slavery** in British India, accomplished in 1843.
 
• **The Morley-Minto reforms refer to the Indian Councils Act of 1909**, which increased the number of Indians in the legislative councils but did not lead to enacting the Government of India Act of 1919.

questions.question: Which is the second largest family in modern Indian languages?

• ** The correct answer is option 4, Dravidian (Dravida), which is the second largest family in modern Indian languages.**
 
• Dravidian languages are spoken in** southern and central India,** as well as parts of Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Nepal, and Bangladesh.
 
• The Dravidian language family includes languages** like Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Malayalam.**
 
• The largest family in modern Indian languages is Indo-European (Aryan), which includes languages like Hindi, Bengali, Punjabi, and Marathi.
 
• Sino-Tibetan (Kirata) and Austric (Nishada) are also language families in India, but they are smaller in size compared to Dravidian and Indo-European.
 
• Sino-Tibetan languages are spoken in the northeastern parts of India, while Austric languages are spoken in central and eastern India.
